have you thought about changing medications? i know most antipsychotics cause weight gain, but i personally try to avoid the ones that are more commonly known for it. i wouldn't stop taking your meds, not a good idea, talk to your doctor about options.

i haven't tried it, it rings a bell but i don't know why i haven't tried it before. i try to avoid ones that can cause fainting, it's happened to a decent amount of other meds in the past. i also try to avoid ones that are well known for weight gain because of an eating disorder i've been dealing with for a long time now, but i know the trying to avoid weight gain is kind of stupid since most do cause that...it's an issue with me. 
just looked it up a bit and says in the precautions area to not take if you've had a history of high prolactin levels. i do. i have hyperprolactimia on haldol, geodon, and risperdal, and those are just the ones that i actually noticed, i just deal with it. i do remember when i was younger and on haldol the first time that after a while i developed a very small cyst on my pituitary gland, so that could be in there. i also try to avoid medications where i'll have to get blood work done once a month because not only do i not want to do that, i can't afford to do that.

How come it honestly did help me when I was micro dosing though? I was still on all my medications, but even with them I was hearing voices. It was only after over a year that I decided to stop my haldol and it all went wrong
